chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one performing Itikaaf going to his wife, so he said: He should not go to his wife at night nor during the day while he is performing Itikaaf.
ai.seo_question: Can a person performing Itikaaf visit their spouse during the retreat?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of Itikaaf is defined by strict seclusion, prohibiting even conjugal relations with one's wife to ensure undivided spiritual focus. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that Itikaaf requires physical and relational isolation within the mosque boundaries, distinguishing it from mere prayer. The prohibition applies continuously, whether the individual is awake or sleeping, emphasizing the sanctity of the retreat period.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, froom Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked himasws about the one performing Itikaaf going to his wife. So heasws said: ‘He should neither go to his wife at night, nor at daytime, while he is performing Itikaaf’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who engages in sexual relation with his wife in ‘Itikaf. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not go to his wife in ‘Itikaf in the day or night while he is in ‘Itikaf.’”
